area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a ranch, a split-level and a restaurant
area.scope.1.why: Most Niles houses went up in the 1950s and 60s; some still run older furnaces and others newer ones, so the age changes the job.
area.scope.2.why: In a split-level the furnace often sits on the lower level, and the upstairs rooms can run warmer in summer.
area.scope.3.why: Condensers sit in narrow side yards beside ranches and split-levels, which sets how a replacement comes in.
area.scope.4.why: Restaurants along Milwaukee Ave run kitchen exhaust and make-up air with the rooftop units, so work is booked around service hours.
area.scope.5.why: Offices and stores on Touhy and around Golf Mill run rooftop units, so roof access and business hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.faq.heading: Niles HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the furnace in my Niles ranch worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.2.q: Do you come out to Niles from Chicago?
area.faq.3.q: Do you service restaurants on Milwaukee Avenue?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC work in Niles need a permit?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the furnace has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. For a restaurant on Milwaukee, tell us your service hours.

extras.faq.2.a: Yes. Niles is on our service area list, about 9 miles north-west of the shop at 1225 N Cleaver St, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Commercial repairs and make-up air are on our list of services. Tell us your service hours when you call, so we can work around them.
extras.faq.4.a: It depends on the job. The Village of Niles sets its own permit rules, mostly for installs and replacements. A repair or tune-up is a different job. Ask whoever quotes an install who pulls the permit.
